title: JSON View
lede: Render JSON objects and arrays as a collapsible tree with syntax coloring, keyboard navigation, search highlighting, and selectable text.

examples.heading: Default
examples.description: JSON View expands levels strictly below `defaultExpandDepth`. Use `defaultExpandDepth={1}` when the first level helps users scan the object without opening every nested value.

examples.heading: Single line
examples.description: Expanded objects with one short primitive key-value pair render on one line. Nested and long values remain multiline.

examples.heading: Embedded
examples.description: JSON View follows surrounding text before and after expanded fields.

examples.heading: Wrapped
examples.description: Long primitive values use the multiline layout and wrap within the available width.

examples.heading: Collapsed
examples.description: Use `defaultExpandDepth={0}` when the surrounding surface needs to stay compact and users can choose which object to inspect.

examples.heading: Highlighted
examples.description: Use `makeJsonViewHighlightPattern` to build the `highlightPattern` prop from search terms. The pattern highlights matching field names and primitive values.

examples.heading: Nested
examples.description: Client-only shapes at the second level (direct children of the root group, where the map walks the rows), expanded to depth 3 (the default): an expanded nested object and array with their block closing brackets, an empty object (no toggle), single pairs that fit one line (an inline group) and one that does not (a block line wrapper), and search marks on keys, a number, a boolean and null.

examples.heading: Inline kinds
examples.description: Top-level single pairs of every value kind on one line, with search marks on the key and the value.
